target.name: UGPS J0722-0540
target.blurb: One of the coolest T dwarfs (T9), 13 light years away, moving 1 arcsecond a year.

warnings: registered to 4 Gaia stars: frame offset -0.39" E, +0.32" N removed
blended: a catalogued source (W1 16.3) lies 3.8 arcsec from the target, inside the area its position is fitted over, so this epoch is left out of the motion fit

match.verdict: Consistent with a cold brown dwarf, type T8 to Y0 (best match T9).
match.method: Chi-square fits of the SPIFF brown-dwarf templates (Gagné et al., arXiv:2604.22012) and of non-brown-dwarf comparisons (reddened stars, dust, power laws, star plus dust), compared by an information criterion on rescaled chi-square, with a goodness-of-fit gate and a check that the template's molecular bands are actually seen.
match.provisional: A catalogued source (W1 16.3) 4.0 arcsec away may contribute about 22% of the light at these wavelengths, or more; treat the type as provisional.

per_pass.label: Nov 2025
per_pass.reason: SPHEREx detects the object at only 10 wavelengths (1.6 to 4.8 µm), which is too little of the spectrum to classify it.

pass_agreement.sentence: All 2 passes typed on their own agree (1 too faint to type alone).

warnings: Catalogue frame-quality scores were unavailable for the WISE frames from 2010 (cryogenic), 2010-2011 (post-cryogenic), so those frames were checked by their measured pixel noise instead.
2 of 256 SPHEREx spectrum points are left out (2 where the target saturates the detector).
The Gaia DR3 and CatWISE2020 lists were reused from the view built on 15 Nov 2026, because the catalogue services did not answer.
A catalogued source (W1 16.3) 4.0 arcsec away may contribute about 22% of the light at these wavelengths, or more; treat the type as provisional.
1 detection is left out of the motion fit because a catalogued source of similar brightness lies within the area the position is fitted over.

field_movers.sentence: We searched this patch for anything else that moved between 2010 and 2024. We found nothing unexplained. The search also picked up the target itself without being told where it is.
